# Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id

## Problem statement

Every pi session spawned from within a skill — the audit skill's `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `run_audit_in_worktree()` in `audit/audit_pr.py` — is saved under pi's default random session ID, so when debugging an audit run it is impossible to tell which session belongs to which work item or which phase produced it. Skills should pass `--session-id` so every spawned pi session clearly identifies the work item it is for and the action being taken (e.g. `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}`).

## Users

- **Producers/operators** debugging audit runs: want to identify, resume, and inspect the exact pi session for a given work item and phase (`pi --session <id>` / `/resume`).
- **Audit skill maintainers**: want session-per-call isolation (unique ID per call) so parallel/fan-out pi calls never share a session file and never re-trigger the "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" failure mode.
- **Operators of long-running systems**: want stale skill-spawned sessions pruned automatically so `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` does not grow unboundedly.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want each pi session spawned during an audit to carry `--session-id audit-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`, so I can resume the exact session that produced a failed verdict.
- As a maintainer, I want each call to get a unique session (not a shared one), so repeated calls never append into the same session file and never hit the assistant-role continuation error that Ralph's original `--no-session` fix addressed.
- As an operator, I want `audit-*` sessions older than a retention period automatically pruned after each audit run, so the session store stays bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every pi subprocess spawned by the audit skill passes `--session-id` with a unique per-call value. `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` appends `--session-id <id>` to the constructed command; the value is generated in `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` as `audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}` (short uuid = `uuid4().hex[:8]`).
- [ ] `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` passes `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}` for each spawned pi call.
- [ ] Session IDs are unique per call — no two calls share a session file; session-per-call isolation means no "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" errors are introduced.
- [ ] Project-level audits (no work-item id) use a stable placeholder in the id (`audit-project-{short_uuid}` — dedupe the repeated `project` context so the id reads cleanly).
- [ ] Automatic cleanup runs at the end of an audit run (`issue` and `project` commands): session files whose names match the `audit-` prefix and whose mtime is older than the retention period (default 112 days) are pruned from the pi session directory.
- [ ] Retention is configurable via a `--session-retention-days` CLI flag on both subcommands and/or an `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env var (flag wins).
- [ ] Cleanup is conservative: it only removes `audit-`-prefixed sessions — never other pi sessions.
- [ ] Tests verify: (a) `--session-id` appears in every constructed pi command with the expected format, (b) session ids are unique across calls, (c) cleanup prunes only stale `audit-*` files and honors the retention setting, (d) existing cmd-construction tests (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`) are updated and still pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the established Ralph session-per-call precedent (SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB): unique `--session-id` per call, dash-separated `{skill}-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, conservative prefix-scoped cleanup, default retention 112 days.
- Backward compatible: `_call_pi()` gains an optional `session_id: str | None = None` parameter; when unset the command is byte-identical to today (existing direct callers/tests unaffected).
- Cleanup must never touch sessions that do not start with the `audit-` prefix.
- The audit skill's context-reduction invariants (`--no-context-files --no-skills`, self-contained prompts) are untouched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_call_pi()` (line ~1492): `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ optional `--tools`, always `--no-context-files --no-skills`). Sessions are saved under pi's default random IDs.
- `_call_pi_and_maybe_log(issue_id, context, prompt, ...)` (line ~2816) already threads `issue_id` (a work-item id, a child id, or `"project"`) and `context` (e.g. `parent`, `phase2_deep`, `child_ac_fallback`) for debug-log naming, but does not forward them to `_call_pi()`.
- `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` (line ~192): `cmd = ['pi', '-p', '--mode', 'json', f"/audit {wl_id}"]` — `wl_id` is in scope.
- No `--session-id` usage exists anywhere in the skill tree today.
- Session storage: pi saves to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path-slug>--/` (overridable via `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` / `--session-dir`); cleanup should honor the env/flag override when present.
- Existing cmd-construction tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`, ~lines 290–400) assert exact arg lists (`assert args == ["pi", "-p", ...]`) and must be updated.
- No dedicated `audit_pr.py` test file exists; add session-id coverage there or in the audit runner tests.

## Desired change

1. **`_call_pi()`**: add optional `session_id: str | None = None`; when set, append `--session-id <session_id>` to the command (before/with the context-reduction flags).
2. **`_call_pi_and_maybe_log()`**: build `session_id = f"audit-{issue_id}-{context}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and forward to `_call_pi()`.
3. **`audit_pr.py`**: build `f"audit-pr-{wl_id}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and append `--session-id`.
4. **Cleanup**: add a helper that scans the pi session directory (honoring `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`/`--session-dir`) for files whose name starts with `audit-`, prunes those older than the retention period (default 112 days; `--session-retention-days` flag + `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env), and logs pruned count/space. Invoke after `issue` and `project` audit commands complete.
5. **Tests**: update cmd-construction tests; add format/uniqueness assertions and cleanup tests (stale pruning, prefix scoping, retention config precedence).
6. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and code comments documenting the session-id convention and retention.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` (~line 1492) add `--session-id` support; `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` (~line 2816) generate `audit-{id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`; `main()`/`cmd_issue`/`cmd_project` add `--session-retention-days` + cleanup hook
- `skill/audit/audit_pr.py` — `run_audit_in_worktree()` (~line 192) add `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update `TestCallPiEnableTools` cmd assertions; add session-id format/uniqueness + cleanup tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document session-id convention + retention config

## Related work

- **SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB** — "Ralph: Use session-per-call with unique IDs instead of --no-session" (completed): direct precedent — `--session-id` per call, `{skill}-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, 112-day retention cleanup, prefix-scoped pruning.
- **SA-0MQ533A3M003N3ER** — "Document how to execute skills via CLI" (completed): documents the session-per-call pattern for pi subprocess invocations.
- **SA-0MPFD4RWQ009AXJR** — Ralph "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" (completed): the original shared-session failure this design avoids by using unique IDs per call.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: session tagging could expand to every conceivable pi invocation or to a shared `pi_utils` helper refactor. Mitigation: scope is limited to the two existing spawn points; extra ideas are recorded as follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Session accumulation**: unique-per-call sessions accumulate faster than shared ones. Mitigation: retention cleanup is included in this item (default 112 days, `audit-` prefix only).
- **Filename/ID character safety**: work-item ids and context strings are filename-safe alphanumerics/dashes; no sanitization needed beyond the prefix convention.
- **Behavioral change risk**: adding a flag to every spawned command could interact with `--mode json` streaming. Mitigation: identical invocation to Ralph's proven pattern; tests assert command structure; backward-compatible default (`None`).
- **Assumption**: retention default of 112 days and the `--session-retention-days` flag naming follow the Ralph precedent; configurable via env var `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` (no config-file migration needed since the audit skill has no `.ralph.json`-style config).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Session ID uniqueness — shared `audit_<id>` per work item (matches your `intake_<id>` example) vs Ralph-style unique per call (`audit-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`)?" — Answer (user): **1b — Ralph-style unique per call** (`audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`), dash-separated. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope — audit skill only, all current skill pi-spawn points, or audit + documented convention?" — Answer (user): **2b — all current skill pi-spawn points**. Research: a full-tree scan found exactly two spawn points, both in the audit skill: `audit_runner.py::_call_pi` and `audit_pr.py::run_audit_in_worktree`. Source: interactive reply + repo grep.
- Q3: "Cleanup — include session retention pruning in this item or keep out of scope?" — Answer (user): **include in this item**. Source: interactive reply.

# Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: phases `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` and `_phase_fetch_and_cq` fail to use commit references stored only in comments, and treat arbitrary hex found in prose as cherry-pick candidates, producing a spurious merge-gate blocker and a false-negative audit.

Discovered during audit of OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm, `--force` run, work already present in `origin/dev`).

## Symptom

- Work item has no feature branch and no commit in its description; its real implementation commit is referenced only in a comment (e.g. `235ef18` for OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S).
- Merge gate logs `integrating (branch=none, commits=[9b0f...])` then fails: `git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object` and blocks the audit.
- `9b0f500f...` is a *foreign* autiobook reference pinned in the description (reference, not a commit in the owning repo). `235ef18` (the real commit) is never discovered.

## Root cause

1. **Comments not fetched early for merge gate.** `_phase_fetch_and_cq` loads the top-level `comments` from `wl show` into a separate binding, but `ctx.work_item.get("comments", [])` (or the equivalent) is still the default empty list when the merge gate resolves evidence, so commit shas referenced only in comments are never seen. Reproduction: `wl show OSL-... --children --json` has `workItem.comments` absent while top-level `comments` holds the Map commit.

2. **Over-broad hex extraction.** `re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE)` picks up arbitrary hex strings (foreign repo refs, docs examples) and enqueues them as cherry-pick targets. The failing run treated `9b0f500f...` (from `9b0f500f11f...`, an autiobook pin) as a required candidate and failed closed when that object was absent.

3. **Interaction.** Because (1) left `commits=[foreign_hex]`, (2) caused the integration failure path; the item *was* already on `origin/dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`) but was rejected.

## Proposed fix

- Fetch and bind `comments` on `ctx` before `_phase_merge_gate` (or pass `comments` into `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`).
- Filter integration candidates to objects that actually exist or are already ancestors of `origin/dev` (e.g. `git cat-file -e <sha>` / `rev-parse --verify` check, or skip foreign shas that are not ancestors and not branch tips), so that documentation hex cited as reference does not force cherry-pick.
- Optionally, scope hex extraction to producer-attributed commit citations (e.g. `see commit <hex>`) rather than every hex token in prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A work item whose only commit citation is in a top-level comment (no branch, no 7+ hex in description) is correctly merged-gated: evidence resolves the commented commit and `containment` verifies it against `origin/dev`.
2. Hex tokens that are not objects in the owning repo (or are cited only as foreign-repo pinned references, not deliverable commits) do not cause `fatal: bad object` or a spurious merge-gate block.
3. Existing behaviour for feature-branch and description-referenced commits is preserved (regression tests).
4. No new behaviour breaks `wl show` clients: comment binding is done in the audit runner only.

## Evidence

- Failing run (`open_source_llm`, `235ef18` already in `origin/dev`):
  ```
  Merge gate: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S work NOT present in origin/dev — integrating (branch=none, commits=["9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b"])
  git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object
  ```
- Manual verification: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`.
- Stored blocker audit: `wl audit-show OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S --json` (open_source_llm).

## Related

- Proposer work item: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm). See its audit trail and producer-review comment id OSL-C0MTQA3R4E0084LBY.
- Worktree remains at `open_source_llm/.worklog/worktrees/audit-merge-OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S` (remove manually once triaged).
data.title: Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

# Raise full-suite per-command timeout so audit auto-execute can complete

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem Statement

During the automated audit of SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0, the audit runner's automatic
full-suite verification invoked the test skill (`run_tests.py`) to execute the
full suite at HEAD. The pytest command hit the default per-command timeout of
600s and was killed, preventing a green full-suite cache entry from being
produced. This meant audit-dependent ACs could only be marked `partial`.

## Current State

- **`.pi/test-config.json`** already exists with `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}`,
  added under **SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV** (commit 715806bb). The measured full
  suite wall-clock is **~412s**, well within the 1500s timeout.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the `.pi/test-config.json`
  mechanism generically (the `timeoutPerCommand` field, its interaction with
  `suiteCommands`, and how the audit runner honours it).
- A **pre-existing test failure** (`test_plan_helpers.py` — Medium risk no
  longer triggers approval per commit a9d8b8b9, but the test still parametrised
  "Medium") blocks AC6. This is a separate issue.

## Users

1. **Automated agents** (audit skill, test skill) — need the full suite to run
   to completion so audit auto-execute can verify ACs.
2. **Developers** running `/skill:test` — need the timeout to reflect real
   full-suite wall-clock time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`.pi/test-config.json`** exists with `timeoutPerCommand` set to a value
   sufficient for the full suite to finish (current value: 1500s; measured
   wall-clock: ~412s, providing ~3.6x safety margin). No `suiteCommands`
   override — command detection uses existing conventions.
2. `run_tests.py --type full --force` completes within the new timeout at HEAD.
3. The audit runner's auto-execute path honours the override (no 600s kill).
4. The change is project-local: no other repository's timeout is affected; the
   `run_tests.py` default (600s) is unchanged.
5. `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` notes this repo's
   `timeoutPerCommand` override and the rationale for the chosen value.
6. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not raise the global default in `run_tests.py`; use the project-local
  override.
- `.pi/` is project configuration, not agent infrastructure — this change
  adds/modifies only `.pi/test-config.json` and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- **`.pi/test-config.json`** — already exists with `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}`
- **`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`** — needs an addendum noting this
  repo's value and rationale
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — reference only, no change expected

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0** — audit that hit the timeout (AC7 blocked)
- **SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61** — per-project suite extension (`.pi/test-config.json`)
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** — audit auto-execute on cache miss (F3)
- **SA-0MTXLTKFP000ZUZ8** — implement.py finish hardcodes a 600s test timeout (open)
- **SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV** — commit that added `.pi/test-config.json` with 1500s

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` is sufficient. Measured wall-clock is
  ~412s on this machine; under heavy load or CI conditions, suites may take
  longer. 1500s provides ~3.6x margin — adequate but not excessive.
- **Assumption:** No future test additions will cause the suite to exceed 1500s.
  If the suite grows significantly, the timeout should be re-evaluated.
- **Scope creep:** The pre-existing test failure in `test_plan_helpers.py` is
  unrelated to the timeout change. A separate work item should be created to
  fix the stale test parametrisation.
data.title: Raise full-suite per-command timeout so audit auto-execute can complete
